full.description: This image is a high-magnification photomicrograph of intestinal or colonic tissue showing inflammation. The histology reveals a crypt abscess with an influx of acute inflammatory cells, specifically neutrophils. This pattern is characteristic of acute infectious colitis, such as that caused by Campylobacter jejuni or enteroinvasive Escherichia coli.

This finding is indicative of an acute bacterial infection such as enteroinvasive Escherichia coli or Campylobacter jejuni.

random.description: This image is a high-power light micrograph showing a section of gastrointestinal mucosa, likely from the colon. It displays marked mucosal inflammation characterized by dense infiltration of inflammatory cells, including neutrophils, lymphocytes, and plasma cells within the lamina propria. Cryptitis and crypt abscesses are evident, indicating active colitis. These histopathological findings are characteristic of inflammatory bowel disease, such as ulcerative colitis.
